From: Adam Zhou <adam@orchidpay.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Pay - sudden throughput spike + elevated error rate

Mina —

We started seeing a sharp increase in request concurrency from our side around 06:50 PT and within a few minutes our payment verification flow began returning 5xx errors and timing out. Error rate peaked at ~18% and median latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s. This is impacting checkout for a subset of customers (small markets on EU region).

We pulled a short log summary and attached it (orchid_logs_summary.csv). We're pausing new promos until this stabilizes. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an infrastructure-side throttling/queueing issue or model-serving OOMs?

We need an ETA for mitigation. Can you open an executive bridge? Our CTO Meera and SRE alias (orchid-support@orchidpay.com) are on this thread.

Thanks,
Adam
Head of Engineering
Orchid Pay

--

Adam — thanks for the heads up and for the log extract. I'm opening an exec bridge now and looping in on-call infra and runtime. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the spike is coming from a single region / app key or multiple keys? That will help routing decisions.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we'll run in parallel):
- Stand up an exec bridge (15 min) — I'll invite engineering leads, SRE, and account exec.
- Roll traffic to a smaller model variant (fast-fallback) for burst handling.
- Activate conservative concurrency caps for Orchid's API key to protect the cluster.
- Collect runtime logs (GPU memory / OOMs) and autoscaler events (last 30m).

I'll send a consolidated status update to your CTO and our execs after we confirm root cause. Marcus — can you grab the runtime_diagnostics and check for KV cache thrash or OOMs? Laura — can we confirm available dedicated capacity in us-west for a short warm-up?

Subject: Re: Orchid Pay - sudden throughput spike + elevated error rate

On it — I pulled traces from the serving runtime for the last 40 minutes. Preliminary findings:
- Observed high tail memory pressure on several GPU workers servicing Orchid's model variant. A few instances reported ephemeral OOMs and restarted (OOM -> restart -> cached KV invalidation).
- Batching increased unexpectedly due to concurrent short requests, which amplified memory footprint per worker.
- Autoscaler did not scale fast enough because the surge was short and bursty; scale-up latencies ~90–120s.

Immediate actions I can take now:
- Flip traffic to the compatible smaller quantized model variant (orchid-proxy-q4_v2) — this reduces per-token memory by ~40% and should eliminate OOM restarts.
- Apply a conservative concurrency cap for Orchid's API key for the next 30 minutes to level requests and buy time for scale-up.
- Stream runtime_diagnostics.pdf (attached) with per-host mem/oom timestamps for postmortem.

If we flip model variants, expect a small change in output distribution; we should keep the customer in the loop. Mina, I'll be ready to flip on your mark.

— Marcus
Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Orchid Pay — incident status and next steps (summary)

Adam / Meera — thank you for the quick report and patience. Short update and agreed actions: 

Summary of impact:
- Start: 2027-03-30T06:50:00 PT. Peak error-rate ~18%, median latency up to ~1.8s for checkout calls. Impacted customers: subset of EU checkouts routed through our us-west cluster.

What we did (timeline):
- 07:15 — exec bridge opened; infra and ops triaged.
- 07:23 — Marcus identified memory pressure and OOM restarts on several workers.
- 07:30 — Flipped traffic for Orchid API key to quantized smaller model variant (orchid-proxy-q4_v2).
- 07:36 — Provisioned 4 dedicated GPUs in us-west as surge capacity (warm-up complete by ~07:40).
- 07:45 — Applied temporary concurrency cap to smooth bursts. Error-rate fell to <1.5% and median latency returned to ~210ms within ~20 minutes of mitigation.

Current status:
- Serving on orchid-proxy-q4_v2 with dedicated nodes attached. Error rates stable; we are monitoring for regressions. No data loss.

Customer-facing note (to share with your teams):
We identified transient memory pressure on shared GPU workers caused by a short burst of concurrent requests. To protect throughput and reduce restarts, we temporarily routed your traffic to a compatible, lower-memory model variant and brought up dedicated capacity for a short window. We will follow up with a technical postmortem and recommended long-term mitigations (traffic shaping, autoscaler tuning, and KV cache sizing).

Action items and owners:
- Marcus: full diagnostic bundle and OOM host list (ETA 4 hours).
- Laura / Ops: cost usage summary and provisional credit documentation (ETA 24 hours).
- Mina: customer-facing incident note + postmortem coordination (ETA 48 hours).

Attachments: status_update_orchid_0330.docx (summary for execs), runtime_diagnostics.pdf, orchid_logs_summary.csv

If you prefer a quick sync with our CTO and your CTO, we can schedule a 20-minute bridge at 14:00 PT to walk through the findings and next steps.

Thanks again — we’ll keep monitoring and reach out if we see any regression.

Best,
